key_insight: Orthogonalizing momentum alone is not enough for nonsmooth optimization: fixed-momentum Muon can fail on convex Lipschitz problems, but an adaptive momentum variant and the proposed MAGD restore convergence guarantees.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued optimization in deep learning and large-scale training, this work clarifies when Muon-like updates are unreliable and provides a practical, dimension-aware alternative with provable rates.
method: Analyze Muon under locally Lipschitz/nonsmooth objectives using a generalized derivative framework.
Construct failure examples showing fixed momentum can miss global optima even with bounded iterates.
Propose MAGD, which blends orthogonalized momentum with gradient information and adaptive weighting to recover convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports synthetic experiments, image classification, and LLM pretraining benchmarks, alongside convex and nonconvex theory with an optimal dimension-dependent lower bound.
watch_item: MAGD’s guarantees rely on boundedness and regularity assumptions, so careful step-size and momentum scheduling is required in practice.
